## 12-Month California Office Lease Review
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg

A 12-month lease is short enough that small wording changes can have a big cost impact. For a California office lease starting **2026-09-01**, the biggest risk areas are **rent increases, repair duties, sublease limits, deposits, and early-exit rules**.

## Lease Clauses to Check Before You Sign
| Clause | What to review | Plain-English check |
|---|---|---|
| Rent escalation | When rent can increase, how much, and whether the increase is fixed or tied to an index | Confirm the base rent for the full 12 months, and look for any scheduled increase, pass-through, or “market adjustment” language |
| Maintenance responsibilities | Who handles HVAC, plumbing, electrical, roof, common areas, pest control, and janitorial service | Make sure the lease clearly says what the landlord fixes and what your business must maintain or pay for |
| Subleasing | Whether you can sublet part or all of the space, and whether landlord consent is required | Check if consent can be “reasonably withheld” and whether you can assign the lease if you sell the business |
| Deposit terms | Security deposit amount, when it can be used, and when it must be returned | Verify the deposit is capped in the lease, what deductions are allowed, and the return deadline after move-out |
| Termination clauses | Your right to end early, landlord’s right to terminate, and default notice periods | Look for cure periods, penalties, and whether you can exit for relocation, shrinking space needs, or business closure |
| Renewal / holdover | What happens if you stay after the term ends | Check holdover rent, notice deadlines, and whether renewal is automatic or requires written notice |
| Operating expenses | CAM, taxes, insurance, utilities, and admin fees | Confirm exactly which extra charges are passed through and whether there is a cap or estimate |

## Plain-English Review Checklist
- **Rent:** Is the monthly amount fixed for all 12 months, or can it rise during the term?
- **Escalation:** If rent increases, is the formula clear and capped?
- **Repairs:** Does the landlord cover major building systems, or could you be paying for expensive repairs?
- **Maintenance:** Are you responsible for routine service only, or also hidden items like HVAC replacement?
- **Subleasing:** Can you sublease without major restrictions if your space needs change?
- **Deposit:** How much is held, what can be deducted, and how fast must it be returned?
- **Termination:** Can you leave early, and if so, what notice and fee apply?
- **Default:** How much time do you get to fix a missed payment or other issue before termination?
- **Move-out:** What condition must the office be in, and are you responsible for restoration?
- **Renewal:** Do you need to give written notice to avoid an automatic extension or holdover rent?

## Questions to Ask the Landlord Before Signing
- Can you confirm the **exact monthly rent for the full 12 months** and whether any increase applies?
- Who pays for **HVAC, plumbing, electrical, pest control, and routine repairs**?
- Are **subleasing and assignment** allowed, and what approval is required?
- How much is the **security deposit**, what can be deducted, and when is it returned?
- What are the **early termination** options, fees, and notice requirements?
- What happens if there is a **late payment or default**?
- Are there any **CAM, tax, insurance, or utility pass-throughs** beyond base rent?
- What are the **move-out and restoration** requirements at lease end?
